purpose: Primary-source material-field evidence batch for Sweden study, Finland employed-person work, and Luxembourg salaried-worker routes.
policy: Only exact route claims supported by current official sources are included; promotion still requires evidenceIds and complete material-field coverage.

records.claim: Sweden's higher-education study residence permit requires final admission to full-time, on-site studies, payment of applicable tuition before applying, and the other applicable residence-permit conditions.
records.methodology: Direct review of current Swedish Migration Agency higher-education residence-permit guidance.

records.claim: For Swedish higher-education study residence-permit applications made in 2026, the maintenance requirement is at least SEK 10,656 per month, subject to specified reductions where free housing or food is provided and higher amounts for accompanying family members.
records.methodology: Direct review of current Swedish Migration Agency maintenance requirements for 2026 applications.

records.claim: Finland offers a residence permit for an employed person (TTOL); the applicant must have qualifying employment and meet the applicable employment-based residence conditions, including sufficient income.
records.methodology: Direct review of current Finnish Immigration Service employed-person residence-permit guidance.

records.claim: For Finland's residence permit for an employed person (TTOL), total gross salary must be at least EUR 1,600 per month in 2026, excluding certain supplements; the salary must also satisfy the applicable collective-agreement requirement.
records.methodology: Direct review of current Finnish Immigration Service 2026 income requirements for employed persons.

records.claim: A third-country national seeking to work in Luxembourg as a salaried worker for more than three months generally needs a temporary authorisation to stay before entry, followed by the applicable residence permit; the employer must complete the required vacancy declaration and recruitment process with ADEM unless an applicable exemption applies.
records.sourceAuthority: Guichet.lu / Luxembourg Ministry of Home Affairs
records.methodology: Direct review of current Luxembourg government guidance for third-country salaried workers.

records.claim: Luxembourg employment remuneration must not fall below the applicable social minimum wage; the applicable minimum is increased for skilled workers, while collective agreements can establish applicable salary scales.
records.methodology: Direct review of Luxembourg government social-minimum-wage guidance; no unsupported universal numeric salary is asserted.
